-- | A Haskell-to-Verilog/VHDL compiler, the Hyle backend
--   
--   The ReWire backend. The Hyle bit-level IR, its checker, optimizer,
--   interpreter, and parser, and the Verilog, VHDL, and Cryptol RTL
--   backends. Builds on rewire-base for shared utilities.
@package rewire-backend
@version 2.8


-- | Abstract syntax for the fragment of Cryptol emitted by the Cryptol
--   backend (ReWire.Hyle.ToCryptol). The generated file is a
--   self-contained named module (Cryptol allows loading it under any file
--   name): a few helper definitions implementing Hyle primitives, an
--   optional <tt>parameter</tt> block declaring externs as uninterpreted
--   functions, and one function per Hyle defn. Helper names contain a tick
--   (<tt>rw'resize</tt>) so they can never collide with generated names
--   (see <a>cryptolName</a>).
module ReWire.Cryptol.Syntax
type Name = Text
type Size = Word

-- | Maps a Hyle name to a valid Cryptol identifier body: any character
--   outside <tt>[A-Za-z0-9_]</tt> becomes an underscore. Callers are
--   expected to prepend a prefix (<tt>rw_</tt>), so the first character
--   doesn't matter and the result can never collide with a Cryptol
--   keyword, a Prelude name, or the tick-containing helper names. The one
--   unprefixed use is the module name (<a>ReWire.Hyle.ToCryptol</a> via
--   <a>modName</a>), where a keyword-named <tt>--top</tt> would emit an
--   invalid module header.
cryptolName :: Text -> Name
data Module
Module :: !Name -> ![Text] -> ![Param] -> ![Defn] -> Module

-- | Cryptol allows loading a file whose name doesn't match.
[modName] :: Module -> !Name

-- | Header comment lines.
[modComments] :: Module -> ![Text]

-- | Externs, as uninterpreted functions.
[modParams] :: Module -> ![Param]
[modDefns] :: Module -> ![Defn]

-- | Helper definitions emitted with every module, implementing Hyle
--   primitives that don't map directly to a Cryptol operator.
--   <tt>rw'resize</tt> truncates or zero-extends to the new width.
helpers :: Doc an

-- | An uninterpreted function declared in a <tt>parameter</tt> block:
--   name, argument widths, result width.
data Param
Param :: !Name -> ![Size] -> !Size -> Param
ppParams :: [Param] -> Doc an

-- | Sequence lengths in types: the device's quantified variable
--   <tt>n</tt>, or <tt>1 + n</tt>.
data Len
LenVar :: Len
LenSucc :: Len
data Ty

-- | <pre>
--   [w]
--   </pre>
TBits :: !Size -> Ty

-- | <pre>
--   [n]t
--   </pre>
TSeq :: !Len -> !Ty -> Ty
ppFun :: [Ty] -> Ty -> Doc an
data Defn
Defn :: ![Text] -> !Name -> !Bool -> ![(Name, Ty)] -> !Ty -> !Exp -> ![Bind] -> Defn
[defnComments] :: Defn -> ![Text]
[defnName] :: Defn -> !Name

-- | Prefix the signature with <tt>{n} (fin n) =&gt;</tt>.
[defnQuantN] :: Defn -> !Bool
[defnArgs] :: Defn -> ![(Name, Ty)]
[defnResTy] :: Defn -> !Ty
[defnBody] :: Defn -> !Exp
[defnWhere] :: Defn -> ![Bind]

-- | A <tt>where</tt>-binding with an explicit type annotation.
data Bind
Bind :: !Name -> !Ty -> !Exp -> Bind
data Exp

-- | Sized hex/binary literal (or <tt>(zero : [0])</tt>).
Lit :: !BV -> Exp
Var :: !Name -> Exp

-- | Prefix application: <tt>f e1 e2</tt>.
Call :: !Name -> ![Exp] -> Exp

-- | Application with a type argument: <tt>f`{k} e1 e2</tt>.
TCall :: !Name -> !Natural -> ![Exp] -> Exp
BinOp :: !Name -> !Exp -> !Exp -> Exp
UnOp :: !Name -> !Exp -> Exp

-- | <pre>
--   e @ k
--   </pre>
Index :: !Exp -> !Natural -> Exp
If :: !Exp -> !Exp -> !Exp -> Exp

-- | Bit to <tt>[1]</tt>: <tt>[e]</tt>.
Sing :: !Exp -> Exp

-- | <pre>
--   [ e | x &lt;- e1 | y &lt;- e2 ]
--   </pre>
Comp :: !Exp -> ![(Name, Exp)] -> Exp

-- | <pre>
--   [e1, e2]
--   </pre>
SeqLit :: ![Exp] -> Exp
class Parenless a
parenless :: Parenless a => a -> Bool
mparens :: (Pretty a, Parenless a) => a -> Doc an

-- | Hex when the width is a multiple of four (Cryptol hex literals have a
--   width of exactly four bits per digit), binary otherwise.
ppLit :: BV -> Doc an

-- | Slicing, MSB-first (Cryptol's bit order): <tt>k</tt> bits starting at
--   MSB offset <tt>off</tt> out of a <tt>w</tt>-bit expression. Skips
--   <tt>take</tt>/<tt>drop</tt> when they would be the identity.
slice :: Size -> Size -> Size -> Exp -> Exp

-- | Truncate-or-zero-extend to the given width (the <tt>trunc</tt> and
--   <tt>zext</tt> coercions), as implemented by the emitted
--   <tt>rw'resize</tt> helper.
resize :: Size -> Exp -> Exp

-- | Concatenation, filtering zero-width parts.
cat :: [Exp] -> Exp
nil :: Exp
isNil :: Exp -> Bool
instance GHC.Classes.Eq ReWire.Cryptol.Syntax.Bind
instance GHC.Classes.Eq ReWire.Cryptol.Syntax.Defn
instance GHC.Classes.Eq ReWire.Cryptol.Syntax.Exp
instance GHC.Classes.Eq ReWire.Cryptol.Syntax.Len
instance GHC.Classes.Eq ReWire.Cryptol.Syntax.Module
instance GHC.Classes.Eq ReWire.Cryptol.Syntax.Param
instance GHC.Classes.Eq ReWire.Cryptol.Syntax.Ty
instance ReWire.Cryptol.Syntax.Parenless ReWire.Cryptol.Syntax.Exp
instance Prettyprinter.Internal.Pretty ReWire.Cryptol.Syntax.Bind
instance Prettyprinter.Internal.Pretty ReWire.Cryptol.Syntax.Defn
instance Prettyprinter.Internal.Pretty ReWire.Cryptol.Syntax.Exp
instance Prettyprinter.Internal.Pretty ReWire.Cryptol.Syntax.Len
instance Prettyprinter.Internal.Pretty ReWire.Cryptol.Syntax.Module
instance Prettyprinter.Internal.Pretty ReWire.Cryptol.Syntax.Ty
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show ReWire.Cryptol.Syntax.Bind
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show ReWire.Cryptol.Syntax.Defn
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show ReWire.Cryptol.Syntax.Exp
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show ReWire.Cryptol.Syntax.Len
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show ReWire.Cryptol.Syntax.Module
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show ReWire.Cryptol.Syntax.Param
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show ReWire.Cryptol.Syntax.Ty

module ReWire.Hyle.Mangle
mangle :: Text -> Text

-- | Mangle a Hyle name into an identifier acceptable to the RTL backends
--   (when it isn't one already): alphanumerics plus underscores and dollar
--   signs (the VHDL pretty-printer further escapes names as needed).
mangleFresh :: Text -> Text

-- | Module names need to be de-conflicted because they aren't immediately
--   freshened.
mangleMod :: Text -> Text

-- | Pick an unused RTL identifier from an already-mangled seed, updating
--   the used map: the seed itself when free, otherwise the first free
--   suffix-numbered variant. Every picked (or <a>seedNames</a>-seeded)
--   name is a key of the map, so a suffixed pick can never collide with a
--   name issued later under its own seed; the value is the seed's next
--   suffix number, keeping repeated requests O(1).
pickFresh :: Text -> HashMap Text Int -> Text -> (Text, HashMap Text Int)

-- | Seed a <a>pickFresh</a> used map with ambient names (ports, registers)
--   that are emitted verbatim, without passing through the backend's
--   fresh-name supply: generated names must not collide with them.
seedNames :: [Text] -> HashMap Text Int

-- | Strip the freshening suffixes stacked onto a name by the Hyle inliner
--   (<tt>$i&lt;digits&gt;</tt>) and the fold-time instance hoist
--   (<tt>$h&lt;digits&gt;</tt>), recovering the original base for display.
--   Suffix groups stack (deep inline chains re-freshen already-freshened
--   names, and hoisting re-lets inliner names), so stripping repeats; a
--   name that is nothing but suffix (e.g. a bare legacy <tt>$i0</tt>) is
--   kept unstripped rather than emptied.
stripFreshTag :: Text -> Text

-- | SystemVerilog reserved words (IEEE 1800-2012, Annex B): generated
--   Verilog identifiers must dodge them. (The VHDL backend needs no
--   analogue: its pretty-printer escapes reserved words as extended
--   identifiers.)
svReserved :: Text -> Bool


-- | The Hyle IR: a pure, first-order, monomorphic, total language over
--   width-indexed bitvectors, plus a synchronous device construct
--   (registers, sequential-extern instances, parallel wire equations). The
--   syntax and semantics are specified in doc/hyle.md; this module is the
--   AST and the pretty printer for the concrete syntax (doc/hyle.md,
--   section 10).
module ReWire.Hyle.Syntax
type Size = Word
type Index = Word
type Name = Text
type GId = Text
type Value = Integer
class SizeAnnotated a
sizeOf :: SizeAnnotated a => a -> Size

-- | Primitive operations (doc/hyle.md, section 3.3). Static parameters
--   (target widths, replication counts) are part of the operator.
data Op
Add :: Op
Sub :: Op
Mul :: Op
UDiv :: Op
UMod :: Op
Pow :: Op
And :: Op
Or :: Op
XOr :: Op
Not :: Op
Shl :: Op
LShr :: Op
AShr :: Op
Eq :: Op
Ne :: Op
ULt :: Op
ULe :: Op
UGt :: Op
UGe :: Op
SLt :: Op
SLe :: Op
SGt :: Op
SGe :: Op
RedAnd :: Op
RedOr :: Op
RedXOr :: Op
ZExt :: !Size -> Op
SExt :: !Size -> Op
Trunc :: !Size -> Op
Rep :: !Natural -> Op

-- | The operator name in the concrete syntax (static arguments printed
--   separately).
opName :: Op -> Text

-- | The typing rule for each operator (doc/hyle.md, section 3.3): given
--   the operand widths, the result width, or Nothing if the operands are
--   ill-typed.
opResultSize :: Op -> [Size] -> Maybe Size
data Exp
Lit :: Annote -> !BV -> Exp
Undef :: Annote -> !Size -> Exp
Var :: Annote -> !Size -> !Name -> Exp
Cat :: Annote -> !Exp -> !Exp -> Exp

-- | e[offset +: width], LSB-indexed.
Slice :: Annote -> !Index -> !Size -> !Exp -> Exp
Prim :: Annote -> !Size -> !Op -> ![Exp] -> Exp
Call :: Annote -> !Size -> !GId -> ![Exp] -> Exp

-- | Combinational extern call with generic arguments.
XCall :: Annote -> !Size -> !Name -> ![Natural] -> ![Exp] -> Exp
If :: Annote -> !Size -> !Exp -> !Exp -> !Exp -> Exp
Let :: Annote -> !Size -> !Name -> !Exp -> !Exp -> Exp
data Sig
Sig :: Annote -> ![Size] -> !Size -> Sig
data Defn
Defn :: Annote -> !GId -> !Sig -> ![Name] -> !Exp -> !Bool -> !Blind [Text] -> Defn
[defnAnnote] :: Defn -> Annote
[defnName] :: Defn -> !GId
[defnSig] :: Defn -> !Sig

-- | Same length as the Sig's argument list.
[defnParams] :: Defn -> ![Name]
[defnBody] :: Defn -> !Exp

-- | Exempt from backend inlining (including --flatten); a real attribute,
--   visible to Eq.
[defnNoInline] :: Defn -> !Bool

-- | Display-only doc lines (<tt>--|</tt>); invisible to
--   Eq<i>Ord</i>Hashable.
[defnDoc] :: Defn -> !Blind [Text]

-- | Sequential externs carry the names of their clock and reset ports
--   (either may be absent); combinational externs have neither.
data ExternKind
Comb :: ExternKind
Seq :: !Maybe Name -> !Maybe Name -> ExternKind
data Extern
Extern :: Annote -> !Name -> ![Name] -> !ExternKind -> ![(Name, Size)] -> ![(Name, Size)] -> !Maybe GId -> Extern
[extAnnote] :: Extern -> Annote
[extName] :: Extern -> !Name
[extGenerics] :: Extern -> ![Name]
[extKind] :: Extern -> !ExternKind
[extInputs] :: Extern -> ![(Name, Size)]
[extOutputs] :: Extern -> ![(Name, Size)]

-- | Combinational externs only.
[extModel] :: Extern -> !Maybe GId

-- | The width of a call to the extern: its outputs, concatenated.
externResultSize :: Extern -> Size
data Register
Register :: Annote -> !Name -> !Size -> !BV -> Register
data Instance

-- | Instance name, extern name, generic arguments.
Instance :: Annote -> !Name -> !Name -> ![Natural] -> Instance
data Stmt
SLet :: Annote -> !Name -> !Exp -> Stmt
SOutput :: Annote -> !Name -> !Exp -> Stmt
SNext :: Annote -> !Name -> !Exp -> Stmt

-- | Instance name, port name.
SInstIn :: Annote -> !Name -> !Name -> !Exp -> Stmt
data Device
Device :: Annote -> !Name -> ![(Name, Size)] -> ![(Name, Size)] -> ![Register] -> ![Instance] -> ![Stmt] -> !Blind [(Text, Integer)] -> Device
[devAnnote] :: Device -> Annote
[devName] :: Device -> !Name
[devInputs] :: Device -> ![(Name, Size)]
[devOutputs] :: Device -> ![(Name, Size)]
[devRegisters] :: Device -> ![Register]
[devInstances] :: Device -> ![Instance]
[devBody] :: Device -> ![Stmt]

-- | Display names for the <tt>__resumption_tag</tt> register's values;
--   invisible to Eq<i>Ord</i>Hashable.
[devTags] :: Device -> !Blind [(Text, Integer)]
data Program
Program :: ![Extern] -> ![Defn] -> !Device -> Program
[progExterns] :: Program -> ![Extern]
[progDefns] :: Program -> ![Defn]
[progDevice] :: Program -> !Device

-- | Display metadata invisible to equality, ordering, and hashing:
--   wrapping a field in <a>Blind</a> keeps doc lines and tag tables from
--   perturbing dedupe keys, memo keys, or the optimizer's fixpoint test
--   (the same convention as <a>Annote</a> itself, for metadata that isn't
--   an annotation).
newtype Blind a
Blind :: a -> Blind a
[unBlind] :: Blind a -> a

-- | The unique width-0 value.
nil :: Exp
isNil :: Exp -> Bool

-- | Concatenate a list of expressions, dropping width-0 components.
cat :: [Exp] -> Exp

-- | Flatten nested concatenations, dropping width-0 components.
gather :: Exp -> [Exp]

-- | Keywords and operator names: rejected as bare identifiers by the
--   parser, and printed quoted when used as identifiers.
reservedWords :: HashSet Text

-- | Parser for the Hyle concrete syntax (doc/hyle.md, section 10).
--   
--   The concrete syntax does not carry per-node widths, so parsing is
--   followed by an elaboration pass that reconstructs the cached sizes
--   bottom-up: variable sizes from binders, call result sizes from the
--   signatures of the named defns and externs. Full well-formedness
--   checking (ReWire.Hyle.Check) is separate; elaboration only fails where
--   a size cannot be reconstructed at all.
module ReWire.Hyle.Parse
parseHyle :: (MonadError AstError m, MonadIO m) => FilePath -> m Program
parseHyleText :: MonadError AstError m => Text -> FilePath -> m Program

-- | Parse a defns-only Hyle fragment (no device declaration): the
--   interchange format for definitions generated outside the fold (the
--   rwcry Cryptol translator). The fragment must be self-contained --
--   elaboration resolves calls against the fragment's own definitions (and
--   externs, if any) only.
parseHyleDefns :: MonadError AstError m => Text -> FilePath -> m [Defn]


-- | The Hyle interpreter: a direct transcription of the denotational
--   semantics in doc/hyle.md (sections 5 and 6). The device denotes a
--   Mealy stream function: registers start at their initial values,
--   outputs and next-register values are computed from the body's
--   equations each cycle.
--   
--   Programs containing instances (sequential externs) or calls to
--   model-less combinational externs cannot be evaluated.
module ReWire.Hyle.Interp
interp :: forall (m :: Type -> Type). MonadError AstError m => Config -> Program -> MealyT m Ins Outs
evalExp :: MonadError AstError m => IEnv -> HashMap Name BV -> Exp -> m BV

-- | Primitive denotations (doc/hyle.md, section 5.2).
evalOp :: MonadError AstError m => Annote -> Op -> [BV] -> m BV
data IEnv
IEnv :: HashMap GId Defn -> HashMap Name Extern -> IEnv
[envDefns] :: IEnv -> HashMap GId Defn
[envExterns] :: IEnv -> HashMap Name Extern

-- | Per-cycle input values and output bitvectors, by wire name.
type Ins = HashMap Name Value
type Outs = HashMap Name BV

-- | Runs non-interactively: given a stream of inputs, produces a stream of
--   outputs.
run :: MonadIO m => Config -> MealyT m Ins Outs -> [Ins] -> m [Outs]

-- | The inclusive bit range [i, j] of a bitvector.
subRange :: (Int, Int) -> BV -> BV

-- | The value driven onto an input wire for a cycle (interp-style inputs:
--   missing wires are driven to zero; values are truncated to the wire
--   width).
inputValue :: Size -> Ins -> Name -> Value

-- | Per-cycle output records in the interpreter's YAML format: the first
--   output prefixed with "- ", the rest indented, in port order.
yamlPrefixes :: [Text]


-- | Well-formedness checking for Hyle programs (doc/hyle.md, section 4):
--   syntax-directed expression typing (every node's cached width is
--   verified), declaration well-formedness, device scoping and
--   exactly-once assignment coverage, and acyclicity of the call graph
--   (including extern-model edges).
module ReWire.Hyle.Check
check :: MonadError AstError m => Program -> m Program


-- | The Cryptol backend on Hyle: the width-preserving embedding of
--   doc/hyle.md, section 8.4. Every Hyle defn becomes a Cryptol function
--   over bitvectors; the device becomes a step function <tt>rw_step</tt>
--   (registers and inputs to outputs and next-register values, as one
--   concatenated vector) wrapped in the standard Mealy stream idiom
--   <tt>rw_device</tt>, matching the Hyle interpreter bit for bit.
--   
--   Because Hyle widths are explicit and exact, no width reconstruction
--   happens here: slices flip to Cryptol's MSB-first order, division gets
--   the SMT-LIB division-by-zero guard (doc/hyle.md, section 5.2), and
--   coercions and reductions map to small fixed helpers; everything else
--   is a per-construct template.
--   
--   Combinational externs without models become uninterpreted functions in
--   a <tt>parameter</tt> block (generic arguments become leading 32-bit
--   arguments); externs with models become ordinary calls to the model's
--   function. Devices with instances (sequential externs) are rejected: a
--   pure target has no equivalent.
module ReWire.Hyle.ToCryptol
compileProgram :: MonadError AstError m => Config -> Program -> m Module


-- | Hyle-to-Hyle transformations: defn inlining (the uses-at-most-once
--   heuristic, plus flatten-everything), dead-defn purging, the
--   <tt>--rtl-opt</tt> optimization fixpoint (partial evaluation,
--   zero-width purging, dedupe), and hoisting clocked-extern calls into
--   device instances. Inlining is sound by the substitution property
--   (doc/hyle.md, section 7); bound names in inlined bodies are freshened
--   to avoid capture. Defns are processed callee-first (the call graph is
--   acyclic), so chains of single-use defns collapse fully.
module ReWire.Hyle.Transform

-- | Inline definitions into their call sites: all of them when
--   <tt>flatten</tt>, otherwise those used at most once. Definitions
--   referenced as extern models are never inlined (the reference is by
--   name), and neither are defns marked noinline -- the pin wins over
--   <tt>--flatten</tt>, so a noinline defn is always findable as a module
--   in the output. The inlined-away defns are removed by the final purge;
--   a follow-up partialEval fuses the slice/concat plumbing exposed by
--   inlining and drops the argument wires that fusion leaves unused.
inline :: Bool -> Program -> Program

-- | Inline definitions satisfying the predicate into their call sites.
inlineBy :: (GId -> Bool) -> Program -> Program

-- | Drop defns unreachable from the device body (following calls and the
--   models of called externs) and extern decls that are never referenced.
--   Not gated on noinline: pinning affects inlining, not liveness, so dead
--   pinned defns don't accumulate.
purgeUnused :: Program -> Program

-- | Constant folding and wire fusion. Primitives, muxes, slices, and
--   concatenations of literals fold via the interpreter's own evaluator;
--   calls (and extern calls with models) whose arguments are all literals
--   evaluate fully. Lets bound to atomic expressions (literals, variables,
--   don't-cares) substitute away; lets bound to pure wiring (slices and
--   concatenations of atoms) are fused through where they are sliced, so
--   slice-of-concat plumbing simplifies across named wires (both
--   expression lets and device-level wires). Unused expression lets are
--   dropped here; unused device wires are dropped by <a>purgeDevLets</a>.
partialEval :: Program -> Program

-- | Drop device wires (SLets) never read by a later statement (fusion in
--   <a>partialEval</a> is what strands them).
purgeDevLets :: Program -> Program

-- | Drop zero-width parameters (and the corresponding arguments at call
--   sites) and zero-width-result defns (calls to them become nil).
purgeZeroWidth :: Program -> Program

-- | Redirect calls to definitions with identical signatures and bodies to
--   a single representative. Should be followed by purgeUnused. Defns
--   marked noinline are name-pinned: they take no part in merging (neither
--   as survivors nor as redirected losers). Each survivor records the
--   losers redirected to it with an appended "also: ..." doc line.
dedupe :: Program -> Program

-- | The standard optimization pipeline, iterated to a fixpoint (bounded by
--   the --rtl-opt level).
optimize :: Natural -> Program -> Program

-- | Defns containing (transitively) calls to sequential externs are
--   inlined into the device body; sequential-extern calls in the device
--   body then become instances: nested lets are flattened to device-level
--   lets (sound: the language is pure and total) and each seq-XCall is
--   replaced by the concatenation of a fresh instance's output ports, with
--   its inputs driven from the call's arguments.
hoistInstances :: MonadError AstError m => Program -> m Program


-- | The rw_helpers VHDL package, embedded at compile time from
--   rewire-backend/vhdl/rw_helpers.vhdl. It implements the Hyle primitive
--   denotations of doc/hyle.md, section 5.2 (unsigned operations over
--   std_logic_vector, which has no arithmetic of its own; SMT-LIB division
--   by zero in rw_div/rw_mod). The VHDL backend emits it with every design
--   and calls rw_resize only at the explicit zext and trunc coercions --
--   no assignment resizes implicitly, since operand and result widths are
--   equal by construction everywhere else.
module ReWire.VHDL.Helpers

-- | The contents of vhdl/rw_helpers.vhdl (the path is relative to the
--   rewire-backend package root, where GHC runs during a build).
helpersPackage :: Text


-- | Syntax for the subset of VHDL-2008 emitted by the VHDL backend
--   (ReWire.Hyle.ToVHDL). Everything is typed std_logic_vector;
--   Verilog-style expression semantics (unsigned arithmetic, width rules)
--   are provided by functions in an emitted rw_helpers package.
module ReWire.VHDL.Syntax
type Name = Text
type Size = Word
type Index = Int
newtype Device
Device :: [Unit] -> Device
[devUnits] :: Device -> [Unit]

-- | An entity/architecture pair with its context clause (use clauses,
--   e.g., ieee.std_logic_1164.all; library clauses are derived).
data Unit
Unit :: !Name -> ![Text] -> ![Text] -> ![Port] -> ![Component] -> ![Signal] -> ![Stmt] -> Unit
[unitName] :: Unit -> !Name

-- | Header comment lines, printed above the entity.
[unitComments] :: Unit -> ![Text]
[unitPackages] :: Unit -> ![Text]
[unitPorts] :: Unit -> ![Port]
[unitComponents] :: Unit -> ![Component]
[unitSignals] :: Unit -> ![Signal]
[unitStmts] :: Unit -> ![Stmt]
data Direction
In :: Direction
Out :: Direction
data Port
Port :: !Name -> !Direction -> !Size -> Port

-- | Component declaration: name, integer generic names, ports.
data Component
Component :: !Name -> ![Name] -> ![Port] -> Component

-- | Declarations in the architecture declarative part: signals with an
--   optional initial value, constants, and display-only comment lines.
data Signal
Signal :: !Name -> !Size -> !Maybe BV -> Signal
Constant :: !Name -> !Size -> !BV -> Signal
SigComment :: !Text -> Signal
ppComment :: Text -> Doc an

-- | Newlines in comment text would push the remainder into code position.
sanitizeComment :: Text -> Text
data Stmt
Assign :: !LVal -> !Exp -> Stmt

-- | Selected signal assignment: scrutinee, target, choices, others.
SelAssign :: !Exp -> !LVal -> ![(BV, Exp)] -> !Exp -> Stmt

-- | Sensitivity list (empty: none), variables, body.
Process :: ![Name] -> ![ProcVar] -> ![SeqStmt] -> Stmt

-- | Component, instance label, generic map, port map (empty name:
--   positional).
Instantiate :: !Name -> !Name -> ![(Name, Integer)] -> ![(Name, Exp)] -> Stmt
Comment :: !Text -> Stmt

-- | Process-local variable declarations.
data ProcVar

-- | variable n : line;
LineVar :: !Name -> ProcVar

-- | A selected-assignment choice: the choices are literal bit-strings of
--   exactly the scrutinee's width (never constants or aggregates, for
--   portability).
ppArm :: (BV, Exp) -> Doc an

-- | Sequential statements (process bodies).
data SeqStmt

-- | if/elsif branches, else branch.
SIf :: ![(Cond, [SeqStmt])] -> ![SeqStmt] -> SeqStmt
SAssign :: !LVal -> !Exp -> SeqStmt

-- | wait for n ns;
SWait :: !Natural -> SeqStmt

-- | write(l, ...); writeline(output, l);
SWriteLn :: ![Chunk] -> SeqStmt

-- | std.env.finish;
SFinish :: SeqStmt

-- | A piece of a line written by SWriteLn: a string literal or the
--   hex-string rendering of an expression.
data Chunk
ChunkLit :: !Text -> Chunk
ChunkHex :: !Exp -> Chunk

-- | Conditions appearing in generated processes.
data Cond

-- | name = "bits"
CondEq :: !Name -> !BV -> Cond

-- | rising_edge(name(0))
CondRising :: !Name -> Cond
data LVal
LVName :: !Name -> LVal

-- | name(j downto i): low index i, high index j.
LVRange :: !Name -> !Index -> !Index -> LVal
LVElem :: !Name -> !Index -> LVal
data Exp
Lit :: !BV -> Exp
Var :: !Name -> Exp

-- | name(j downto i): low index i, high index j.
Slice :: !Name -> !Index -> !Index -> Exp

-- | name(i downto i): a 1-bit vector.
Elem :: !Name -> !Index -> Exp
Cat :: ![Exp] -> Exp
FunCall :: !Name -> ![Exp] -> Exp
Num :: !Natural -> Exp

-- | A qualified bit-string literal: hex (std_logic_vector'(X"5a")) when
--   the width is a whole number of hex digits, binary
--   (std_logic_vector'(B"0101")) otherwise.
ppLit :: BV -> Doc an

-- | A literal in signal-initial position: like <a>ppLit</a>, except wide
--   all-zero vectors render as an aggregate.
ppInit :: BV -> Doc an

-- | The value in binary, exactly the vector's width.
ppBits :: BV -> Text

-- | The value in hex, zero-padded to exactly width/4 digits.
ppHex :: BV -> Text
ppVecTy :: Size -> Doc an

-- | Print a name as a VHDL identifier: a basic identifier when valid (and
--   unambiguous: all-lowercase, since basic identifiers are
--   case-insensitive), otherwise a VHDL-2008 extended identifier (\name\).
ppName :: Name -> Doc an
vhdlName :: Name -> Text
reservedWords :: HashSet Text
ppUnit :: Unit -> Doc an

-- | Library clauses are derived from the package names (the work and std
--   libraries are implicit).
ppContext :: [Text] -> Doc an
instance GHC.Classes.Eq ReWire.VHDL.Syntax.Chunk
instance GHC.Classes.Eq ReWire.VHDL.Syntax.Component
instance GHC.Classes.Eq ReWire.VHDL.Syntax.Cond
instance GHC.Classes.Eq ReWire.VHDL.Syntax.Device
instance GHC.Classes.Eq ReWire.VHDL.Syntax.Direction
instance GHC.Classes.Eq ReWire.VHDL.Syntax.Exp
instance GHC.Classes.Eq ReWire.VHDL.Syntax.LVal
instance GHC.Classes.Eq ReWire.VHDL.Syntax.Port
instance GHC.Classes.Eq ReWire.VHDL.Syntax.ProcVar
instance GHC.Classes.Eq ReWire.VHDL.Syntax.SeqStmt
instance GHC.Classes.Eq ReWire.VHDL.Syntax.Signal
instance GHC.Classes.Eq ReWire.VHDL.Syntax.Stmt
instance GHC.Classes.Eq ReWire.VHDL.Syntax.Unit
instance Prettyprinter.Internal.Pretty ReWire.VHDL.Syntax.Chunk
instance Prettyprinter.Internal.Pretty ReWire.VHDL.Syntax.Component
instance Prettyprinter.Internal.Pretty ReWire.VHDL.Syntax.Cond
instance Prettyprinter.Internal.Pretty ReWire.VHDL.Syntax.Device
instance Prettyprinter.Internal.Pretty ReWire.VHDL.Syntax.Direction
instance Prettyprinter.Internal.Pretty ReWire.VHDL.Syntax.Exp
instance Prettyprinter.Internal.Pretty ReWire.VHDL.Syntax.LVal
instance Prettyprinter.Internal.Pretty ReWire.VHDL.Syntax.Port
instance Prettyprinter.Internal.Pretty ReWire.VHDL.Syntax.ProcVar
instance Prettyprinter.Internal.Pretty ReWire.VHDL.Syntax.SeqStmt
instance Prettyprinter.Internal.Pretty ReWire.VHDL.Syntax.Signal

instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show ReWire.VHDL.Syntax.Component
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show ReWire.VHDL.Syntax.Cond
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show ReWire.VHDL.Syntax.Device
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show ReWire.VHDL.Syntax.Direction
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show ReWire.VHDL.Syntax.Exp
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show ReWire.VHDL.Syntax.LVal
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show ReWire.VHDL.Syntax.Port
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show ReWire.VHDL.Syntax.ProcVar
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show ReWire.VHDL.Syntax.SeqStmt
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show ReWire.VHDL.Syntax.Signal
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show ReWire.VHDL.Syntax.Stmt
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show ReWire.VHDL.Syntax.Unit

module ReWire.Verilog.Syntax
newtype Device
Device :: [Module] -> Device
[pgmModules] :: Device -> [Module]
type Name = Text
type Size = Word
type Index = Int
type Value = Integer
data Module

[modName] :: Module -> Name

-- | Header comment lines, printed above the module keyword.
[modComments] :: Module -> ![Text]
[modPorts] :: Module -> [Port]
[modSignals] :: Module -> [Signal]
[modStmt] :: Module -> [Stmt]
ppComment :: Text -> Doc an

-- | Newlines in comment text would push the remainder into code position.
sanitizeComment :: Text -> Text
data Port

-- | can't be reg
Input :: Signal -> Port

-- | can't be reg
InOut :: Signal -> Port
Output :: Signal -> Port
ppDims :: [Size] -> Doc an
data Signal
Wire :: [Size] -> Name -> [Size] -> Signal
Logic :: [Size] -> Name -> [Size] -> Signal
Reg :: [Size] -> Name -> [Size] -> Signal
sigName :: Signal -> Name
data Stmt
Always :: [Sensitivity] -> Stmt -> Stmt
AlwaysComb :: Stmt -> Stmt
Initial :: Stmt -> Stmt
IfElse :: Exp -> Stmt -> Stmt -> Stmt

-- | Scrutinee, case items, default item.

Assign :: LVal -> Exp -> Stmt
SeqAssign :: LVal -> Exp -> Stmt
ParAssign :: LVal -> Exp -> Stmt

-- | Net declaration assignment: wire [n-1:0] x = e;
WireAssign :: Size -> Name -> Exp -> Stmt

-- | A signal declaration in statement position.
Decl :: Signal -> Stmt
LocalParam :: Size -> Name -> BV -> Stmt
Comment :: Text -> Stmt
Block :: [Stmt] -> Stmt
Instantiate :: Name -> Name -> [(Name, Exp)] -> [(Name, Exp)] -> Stmt

-- | #n;
Delay :: Natural -> Stmt

-- | $display("fmt", args);
Display :: Text -> [Exp] -> Stmt

-- | $finish;
Finish :: Stmt
ppItem :: (Exp, Stmt) -> Doc an
data Sensitivity

Neg :: Name -> Sensitivity
data Exp

-- | <pre>

--   </pre>
Signed :: Exp -> Exp

--   </pre>
Unsigned :: Exp -> Exp
LitBits :: BV -> Exp

class Parenless a

mparens :: (Pretty a, Parenless a) => a -> Doc an
ppBinOp :: Exp -> Text -> Exp -> Doc an

-- | The Verilog backend on Hyle. With widths explicit and exact in the IR
--   (doc/hyle.md, G1), expression emission is a per-construct template: no
--   context-width reconstruction, no pattern compilation, no clock
--   plumbing through the module tree (Hyle defns are always pure --
--   sequential externs are device-level instances), and the state machine
--   is built from the device's explicit registers rather than
--   reconstructed from the resumption layout.
--   
--   Defns are emitted one module each (inlining decisions are made
--   upstream by ReWire.Hyle.Transform.inline); the device becomes the top
--   module: per-register current/next signals updated in a single clocked
--   process, wire assignments for the device lets, and one instantiation
--   per sequential-extern instance.
module ReWire.Hyle.ToVerilog
compileProgram :: MonadError AstError m => Config -> Program -> m Device

-- | A testbench driving the device with interp-style inputs and printing
--   outputs each cycle in the interpreter's YAML format (same protocol and
--   timing as the VHDL testbench).
testbench :: Config -> Device -> [Ins] -> Module

-- | Clock and reset port names, when the device has them: no clock when
--   there are no registers and no instances; no reset without a clock.
clockReset :: Config -> [Register] -> [Instance] -> (Maybe Text, Maybe Text)

-- | Display names for a defn module's live (nonzero-width) parameters,
--   shared by the Verilog and VHDL backends: VHDL component declarations
--   must agree with the entity's port names (default binding matches
--   formals to entity ports by name), so both the entity and every call
--   site derive the same list from the defn alone. Each parameter name is
--   stripped of freshening tags and mangled; <tt>arg&lt;i&gt;</tt> is the
--   fallback for names that are SystemVerilog keywords, don't start with a
--   letter or underscore, or duplicate an earlier port (positionally,
--   compared case-folded: VHDL basic identifiers are case-insensitive).
--   The result port is always <tt>res</tt>, seeded into the dedupe so no
--   parameter takes it.
defnPortNames :: Defn -> [Text]

-- | The text after the last <tt>.</tt> of a qualified name (e.g.
--   <tt>main.getIns</tt> -&gt; <tt>getIns</tt>): the seed for instance
--   labels.
lastComponent :: Text -> Text

-- | The register the device's tag table (devTags) names the values of.
tagReg :: Text


-- | The VHDL backend on Hyle, mirroring ReWire.Hyle.ToVerilog (the
--   cosimulation check keeps the two aligned). With widths explicit and
--   exact in the IR, the width-reconstruction machinery of the old backend
--   (<tt>wcast</tt>/<tt>expWidth</tt>) disappears: every emitted
--   expression already has exactly the width its context requires, and the
--   rw_helpers package is needed only for the operations themselves (VHDL
--   std_logic_vector has no arithmetic), not for resizing discipline.
--   
--   Defn modules never take clock or reset ports (sequential externs are
--   device-level instances). Extern ports connect by name; ports left
--   anonymous in the source-level extern descriptor reach this backend
--   with the <tt>p&lt;i&gt;</tt> names synthesized by the producer, which
--   the hand-written VHDL implementations in the test suite already use.
module ReWire.Hyle.ToVHDL
compileProgram :: MonadError AstError m => Config -> Program -> m Device

-- | A testbench driving the device with interp-style inputs and printing
--   outputs each cycle in the interpreter's YAML format (same protocol and
--   timing as the Verilog testbench).
testbench :: Config -> Device -> [Ins] -> Unit
